skill.name: helpdesk-automation
skill.description: Automate HelpDesk ticket review workflows through Rube MCP, including ticket browsing, saved views, canned responses, and custom field inspection.
skill.summary: Guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through read-only HelpDesk workflows using Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around tool names, parameter names, and example fences in SKILL.md. The only confirmed issue is a low-severity external MCP endpoint trust boundary at line 21; no prompt injection, hidden code execution, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Document that Rube MCP is a third-party service and tell users to review provider trust, workspace permissions, and HelpDesk data access before connecting.

static_findings.snippet: - Active HelpDesk connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `helpdesk`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `HELPDESK_LIST_TICKETS` - List tickets with sorting and pagination [Required]
- Forward pagination requires both `next.value` and `next.ID` from previous response
- `silo` determines which folder to list from; default is active tickets
- Response data may be nested under `data` or `data.data`
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Keep page sizes reasonable to avoid timeouts

content.value_statement: Support teams spend time repeating ticket discovery and account checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through read-only HelpDesk workflows using Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Lists HelpDesk tickets from active, archived, trashed, or spam silos.
Explains cursor-based pagination using timestamp and ticket ID cursors.
Lists saved HelpDesk views configured in the HelpDesk interface.
Retrieves canned response templates for support replies.
Lists custom field definitions and explains where field values appear.
Directs agents to search Rube MCP tools first for current schemas.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active HelpDesk connection before use.
Covers read-only list and inspection workflows only.
Does not create, update, move, or reply to tickets.
Depends on current Composio tool schemas returned at runtime.

use_cases.title: Review current support queues
use_cases.description: Browse active or archived tickets with sorted pages and stable cursor navigation.

use_cases.title: Audit response resources
use_cases.description: Check saved views, canned responses, and custom fields before updating team procedures.

use_cases.title: Prepare HelpDesk data summaries
use_cases.description: Collect ticket and configuration context for reporting without changing HelpDesk records.

prompt_templates.title: List recent tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the HelpDesk automation skill to list the most recent active tickets. Search Rube MCP tools first and show the next-page cursor details.

prompt_templates.title: Browse an archive page
prompt_templates.prompt: List archived HelpDesk tickets sorted by last message date. Use a page size of 50 and explain whether another page is available.

prompt_templates.title: Review support templates
prompt_templates.prompt: List available HelpDesk canned responses and summarize what each template appears to be for. Do not edit any templates.

prompt_templates.title: Map HelpDesk configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect saved views and custom fields, then produce a concise operations summary with possible gaps in queue organization.

output_examples.input: Show me the newest active HelpDesk tickets.
output_examples.output: A ticket list sorted by creation time, with each ticket summarized and next-page cursor details included when available.

output_examples.input: What canned responses can our agents use?
output_examples.output: A readable summary of available response templates, including likely purpose and any placeholders that need agent review.

output_examples.input: Which custom fields are configured for tickets?
output_examples.output: A field inventory with names, field types, validation notes, and guidance on where populated values may appear.

best_practices: Confirm the HelpDesk connection is active before running any workflow.
Use moderate page sizes and follow returned cursors exactly.
Treat ticket content, canned responses, and custom fields as sensitive business data.
anti_patterns: Do not skip tool schema discovery before calling Rube MCP tools.
Do not mix forward and backward pagination cursors in one request.
Do not assume this skill can modify tickets or HelpDesk settings.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It guides read-only HelpDesk workflows for ticket lists, views, canned responses, and custom field definitions.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires Rube MCP and an authenticated HelpDesk connection through Composio.

faq.question: Can it create or update tickets?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows are limited to listing and inspecting HelpDesk data.

faq.question: Why should tools be searched first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP schemas can change, so searching first helps the agent use current tool names and parameters.

faq.question: How does pagination work?
faq.answer: Ticket pagination uses timestamp and ticket ID cursor pairs from the previous response.

faq.question: Is ticket data sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. Users should handle ticket content, views, templates, and fields according to their organization policies.
